acceptance_criteria.description: into_parts consumes the response and returns all four exact owned fields, moving the non-Clone ticket without a textual or byte copy.
Existing response construction, strict JSON, matches_request correlation, borrowing accessors, and secret redaction remain unchanged.
Focused/full coop-cloud tests, strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass with only realtime.rs changed.

closed_decisions: Add a public consuming MintRealtimeTicketResponse::into_parts(self) accessor returning realtime version, runtime fence, owned non-Clone RealtimeTicket, and expiry without exposing or copying ticket text.
Callers must still invoke matches_request before consuming the response; the accessor performs no implicit authorization or correlation decision.
Do not remove the existing borrowing accessors or change serialized JSON, constructors, validation, Debug redaction, ticket zeroization, or protocol version.
Test field preservation and ownership transfer without placing plaintext secret material in failure messages.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit any other file, add a Clone implementation, expose ticket bytes/text, serialize a new shape, change response validation, or add launcher/sidecar integration.
Do not stage, commit, branch, fetch, pull, push, contact repository remotes, create or remove worktrees, or revert another worker's edits.
objective: Add a consuming response accessor that moves a minted realtime ticket into its future in-process owner without cloning or re-encoding the secret.

return_when: All acceptance criteria are resolved and every verification outcome is recorded.
Moving the ticket safely requires changing an unowned secret or protocol boundary.
A concrete toolchain or isolated-worktree failure prevents progress within the execution budget.
